name: Gateway 3 · Focus-12-style: expanded awareness
summary: From a stable Focus-10-style state, count on to 11 and 12 and let your awareness widen. Then do a spatial orientation exercise, ask one question you prepared beforehand and, if you like, picture a realistic goal. Monroe described Focus 12 as induced by additional sound patterns; here a 24 Hz beat on 400 Hz is added (carrier and level are our design). Counting, the clock exercise, problem solving and goal patterning follow the 1977 Gateway workbook and the 1983 Army assessment, in our own words. Optional blinded helmet arm: 4 Hz in-phase sine, untested.
setting: Quiet room, dim (not dark) light, reclined or lying down, closed-back stereo headphones (needed for binaural mode; on speakers switch to isochronic mode). Not right after a heavy meal; empty your bladder and silence your phone. Best when you are rested. Never while driving.
cautions: Stop at once (count back and open your eyes, or move a finger) on dizziness, panic, headache or ringing ears. Do not use these sessions if you have epilepsy or photosensitivity, are in a psychiatric crisis or have a hearing problem, unless a doctor agrees. Keep the volume low: WHO advises an average of 80 dB(A) or less and device volume of 60 % or less. No driving, machinery or exams for at least 30 minutes afterwards: theta and delta beats did worse than beta beats on vigilance (Lane et al. 1998) and lowered recall against a noise control (Garcia-Argibay et al. 2019). Sound only; the app never uses flicker. This is an untested composite and not The Monroe Institute's program: no recordings, scripts or affirmation of theirs are used. Not for decisions with legal, medical or financial consequences: answers are subjective. Beta layers can feel nervy; if you tense up, lower the volume (MIAS reported 'intolerable nervousness' from some sound sequences). The helmet arm is experimental and runs only blinded (real or sham, revealed after your ratings): the god-helmet.com Shakti safety page advises against combining the helmet with binaural-beat devices in real time.
unlock: Recommended after at least 3 Focus-10-style sessions with a depth of 5 or more (Monroe's guidepost model).

steps.title: Check-in and volume
steps.instructions:
Put on the headphones the right way round and lie back.

You hear soft pink noise, like distant surf, drifting slowly from side to side. Keep the volume you set at calibration, or turn it down until the sound is quiet and comfortable: the tones that follow are about 15 dB louder than this noise. Stay at or below 60 % device volume.

Try not to watch the step timer during the session. Rate how you feel right now.

steps.title: Prepare one question
steps.instructions: While you are fully awake, write one specific question or problem. The more concrete, the better. It stays on this phone unless you export your runs.

steps.title: Short preparation
steps.instructions:
Close your eyes and go through the preparation at your own pace:

1. **Set-aside box:** turn each worry or task into a simple symbol, put it in a strong container and close the lid.
2. **Breathing:** slow breaths, filling the body region by region from the chest down to the feet; hold only if it is comfortable.
3. **Humming:** one long, steady tone on each out-breath; feel it in your head and chest.

The sound changes when it is time to move on.

steps.title: Focus-10-style: count 1 to 10
steps.instructions:
Count from 1 to 10 and settle into the body-asleep, mind-awake balance.

*Sound: the delta/theta set; after 3 minutes the quiet 16 Hz low-beta layer joins.*

steps.title: Count 11 and 12
steps.instructions:
When the state feels stable, say "eleven" to yourself, then "twelve", as a sense of widening or of alert energy appears. Don't force it. If nothing changes, simply stay where you are: the workbook calls Focus 10 the key.

*Sound: a 24 Hz beat on 400 Hz joins, 12 dB below the main tones (our design).*

steps.title: Clock exercise
steps.instructions:
Imagine you are at the centre of a huge clock face lying flat around you. Send your attention towards 12, then 3, 6 and 9, and notice any impressions.

Then turn the clock so that 3 is in front of you and do it again.

steps.title: Your question
steps.instructions:
Bring your question to mind and really want an answer, for about a minute. Then let go of it completely.

Notice images, words, feelings or a sudden knowing. The answer may also come later: the 1983 Army report mentions two to three days.

steps.title: Goal picture (optional)
steps.instructions: If you like, picture a realistic, beneficial goal as if it were already done, with the feeling that goes with it. Then release the picture outward and let it go. Keep goals modest and fair to others, and don't force anything. Or simply rest.

steps.title: Count back 12, 11, 10
steps.instructions: Count down: twelve, eleven, ten. Rest at ten for a minute.

steps.title: Count back from 10 to 1
steps.instructions: Count slowly from 10 down to 1 and feel more awake with each number. Move your fingers and toes, stretch and open your eyes. Take back what you still want from the box.

steps.title: Journal
steps.instructions: Write down any answer material, perceptions and feelings. Over the next three days, note any late answers in your own journal.

steps.title: Session report
steps.instructions: Fill in the session report while the session is fresh.

steps.title: How you feel now
steps.instructions: Sit up slowly. Rate how you feel now, the same way as at the start.
